business_scope.primary_industry_name: Commercial Mail Receiving Agency (CMRA) and Digital Scanning

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Spain-United Kingdom Trade and Cooperation Agreement

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 10/2010 on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (as amended by Law 7/2021), and Royal Decree 304/2014 regulating the beneficial ownership register

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent issuing authority in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Equivalent

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against EU and Spanish AEAT/Guardia Civil PEP lists, OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated Sanctions List, and domestic sanctions and terrorist financing lists

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (via Colegio de Registradores portal at registradores.org)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Mandatory Spanish language and Latin alphabet; no transliteration permitted
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Agencia de Recepción de Correspondencia Comercial
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: File administrative appeal with the Registro Mercantil within one month of rejection notice; if denied, pursue contentious-administrative judicial review before the Audiencia Nacional or relevant court

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for virtual office and CMRA activities provided a physical address is designated as registered office; however, for regulated mail scanning and digital services, physical presence may be required for licensing and AML compliance
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (5-10% for routine AML/CFT checks; higher for high-risk sectors such as mail handling)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, Texto Refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital; Articles 19–23 (notarial deed and statutory formalities), 58–62 (minimum share capital, contributions and registered office), 106–107 (administrative body), 221–222 (bylaws registration).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (name certification); Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office (inscription of deed); Ministry of Justice through Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (appeals).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución (public deed of incorporation) duly notarized and subsequently recorded in the Registro Mercantil via the official registration application.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The SL requires minimum share capital of EUR 3,000 fully subscribed and paid in cash or non-cash assets at incorporation. Cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked escrow account with a Spanish credit institution in the company's name; the bank issues the certificate of deposit and funds are released to the company only after registration in the Commercial Registry. Non-cash contributions require an expert valuation report where legally required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, the incorporators subscribe and pay up the entire share capital of €3,000 and confirm its deposit in a blocked Spanish bank account for the company's benefit. RESOLVED FURTHER, the registered office is fixed at [Calle, Número], [City], Spain, as the principal administration and receipt address. RESOLVED FURTHER, [Name Surname] is appointed sole administrator and legal representative, with full powers before the Commercial Registry, tax authorities, banks, notaries and public bodies; to obtain the tax ID, open corporate accounts, and execute any licences or permits enabling virtual office and mail scanning services. Approved unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Negative Name Certificate (Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) via Sede Electrónica
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application online with up to three proposed corporate names. The RMC verifies that no identical name is on the register and issues the negative name certificate valid for 3 months. The certificate must be attached to the deed. For the virtual office activity, the name should reflect a neutral professional denomination and not imply regulated financial services.
required_dossiers: Signatures of the founding partners or their electronic certificates
Proposed corporate denomination list (up to three)
Country of registered office and purpose to be included in the certificate
Power of attorney if acting through representative
Legal structure and planned capital statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RMC rejects the name due to similarity or misleading character, resubmit alternative names using the online correction process. If the rejection is final, file a formal review request before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit paid-up capital in a blocked escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution selected by the founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Each founder must deposit at least the amount subscribed into a corporate formation account opened at a Spanish bank in the future company's name. The bank issues a certificate of deposit proving payment of EUR 3,000. The account remains blocked until the company is registered. Non-resident founders must provide proof of source of funds and passport/NIE for AML/KYC compliance.
required_dossiers: Bank KYC forms and AML declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises compliance concerns, provide an enhanced explanatory letter describing the virtual office and CMRA services and sourcing of funds. If the bank still refuses, open alternative banking arrangements with another credit institution or use a notary-authorized escrow service.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the Escritura de Constitución before a Spanish notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary of the chosen notarial district (Colegio Notarial)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founders appear in person or through a lawfully empowered attorney at the notary's office. The notary prepares the public deed from the draft bylaws, the name certificate, and the bank deposit certificate. All parties sign, and the notary reads and authenticates the document. The deed must include the registered office address that will be used for the CMRA and mail scanning operations.
required_dossiers: Bank deposit certificate or expert valuation report
Identity documents of founders and proxies
Completed Model 600 form for AJD tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a defect, the parties correct the issue and re-execute. If the notary refuses to sign, obtain a written explanation and select another notary within the same district to complete the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pay AJD tax and obtain provisional NIF/CIF
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and the Autonomous Community tax treasury
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days after notarial authorization, file Model 600 with the autonomous community tax office to pay stamp duty on the declared capital (0.5%–1.5% depending on region). Simultaneously, apply to AEAT for the provisional NIF/CIF using the notarial deed and presenting Model 036/037. Indicate CNAE 8299 and the virtual office and mail scanning activity.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT requests additional documentation, resubmit within 10 business days. If any tax defect appears, file a rectification Model 036 and pay the corrected tax within 15 days to avoid surcharges.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the company in the Registro Mercantil Provincial
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial competent over the province where the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the first notarial copy, certified copy, provisional NIF, proof of AJD payment, and the registration application to the Provincial Commercial Registry. The registrar verifies the legality and capacity of the deed, checks the name certificate, and issues the inscription. Upon registration the company acquires legal personality. Publication in the BORME follows automatically.
required_dossiers: Registration application signed by the administrator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a calificación negativa (defect), correct the stated issues and resubmit within 2 months. If the refusal is maintained, appeal to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain definitive NIF and complete tax census registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the registry inscription certificate is issued, apply to AEAT to replace the provisional NIF with the definitive NIF. Present the registration certificate and the notarial deed. Update the entrepreneur census through Model 036, confirming the CNAE 8299 and the physical address of the virtual office. Activate the company's electronic certificate for future filings.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the definitive NIF cannot be issued because of mismatched data, submit a rectification Model 036 and re-present the correct registry certificate. AEAT will issue a correction instruction that must be satisfied before final issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with Social Security and establish occupational health and safety
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS) and accredited external prevention service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the company will hire employees, request an employer contribution account number from TGSS, indicating the registered office address. Register the company in the RED system and file worker registrations. Concurrently, contract an external occupational risk prevention service to complete the initial risk assessment and workplace health and safety plan. Even without employees, the administrator must ensure the premises meet Law 31/1995 minimum standards.
required_dossiers: Identity and social security numbers of administrator and employees
Contract with an accredited prevention service
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If TGSS rejects the employer registration, correct the RLT/SRET data and resubmit within 10 days. If the labour authority finds deficiencies in the prevention plan, implement corrective measures and file a revised risk assessment within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain municipal activity license or file a prior communication (licencia de apertura / declaración responsable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ayuntamiento – Department of Urban Planning, Licenses and Activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a declaración responsable or comunicación previa de actividad through the municipal online window, attaching the technical safety and environmental reports. For a low-impact service activity such as mail scanning, no formal environmental impact assessment is required, but the municipal environmental office may register the activity in the local catalogue. If full licencia de apertura is required, submit the plans, pay the municipal fee, and allow the prescribed waiting period before operations begin.
required_dossiers: Deed of incorporation and registry certificate
Technical safety report by an authorized technician
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the council suspends commencement, revise the technical report to address fire, electrical, or accessibility deficiencies and request an extension. If an administrative denial is issued, appeal to the local administrative court within 2 months.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ayuntamiento (City Council) – Department for Urban Planning, Licenses and Activities; for autonomous community supervision of CNAE 8299 service activities: Consejería competente en materia de industria y comercio. A state industrial permit is not required because the activity is non-industrial.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Apertura / Comunicación Previa de Actividad for 'Otras actividades de apoyo a empresas n.c.o.p.' (CNAE 8299), specifically virtual office, commercial mail receiving and digital mail scanning services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Consejería de Medio Ambiente of the Autonomous Community; national supervision by the Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITECO)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / no EIA required. The activity falls under Category 7 (service premises) of the municipal environmental annex in most autonomous communities; no full Environmental Impact Assessment is required under Law 21/2013 because the premises are office-based and have no industrial emissions.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No significant wastewater or VOC emissions expected. Printing and scanning consumables must be managed under Royal Decree 110/2015 (WEEE) and Law 7/2022 (waste). Office waste must be segregated; if paper waste exceeds 25 tonnes per year, a registered waste manager is required. Noise levels must comply with municipal ordinances, typically below 40 dB(A) at the façade.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before opening, submit to the municipal authority a technical report demonstrating compliance with CTE DB-SI (fire safety), low-voltage electrical inspection, emergency exit lighting, and accessibility. A fire safety certificate signed by an authorized technician and a valid building occupancy permit are required. The workplace risk assessment under Law 31/1995 must be available on site; each workstation must meet minimum surface, light, and ventilation conditions under Royal Decree 486/1997.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), including the Sede Electrónica de la AEAT at https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es. The AEAT administers Spanish corporate income tax, value added tax, census registration, tax identification numbers, intra-Community VAT registration and customs-related registrations. Regional tax authorities do not generally administer VAT or corporate income tax in ordinary mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands; the Basque Country and Navarre have separate historical tax regimes, but they are not applicable to an entity registered in ordinary national Spain unless its tax residence or operations fall within those territories.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada must obtain a Spanish Número de Identificación Fiscal (NIF), generally beginning with the letter B for a Spanish limited liability company. The incorporation filing normally includes a provisional NIF request through AEAT using census registration procedures, commonly Modelo 036, supported by the notarial incorporation deed, articles of association, registry or incorporation evidence, and identification of directors and representatives. After registration with the Mercantile Registry, the company must update AEAT and obtain or confirm its definitive NIF by filing the relevant census information and the registered deed. A foreign shareholder or foreign director generally requires an individual or foreign-entity Spanish NIF/NIE as applicable. Foreign shareholders must provide legalized or apostilled corporate documents, certified Spanish translations where required, proof of legal existence, registered address, identity documents, and a power of attorney if an agent files on their behalf. A non-resident foreign entity carrying on taxable activities in Spain must request a Spanish NIF through AEAT, normally using Modelo 036 and appointing a Spanish tax representative where legally required or commercially advisable. VAT registration is performed through the census declaration before the commencement of taxable activities. A company making intra-Community supplies or acquisitions should request inclusion in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios (ROI) and the VIES system through Modelo 036. An entity importing or exporting goods should obtain an Economic Operators Registration and Identification (EORI) number through the Spanish customs administration. Tax registration does not replace any municipal, sectoral, data-protection, electronic-communications, postal, consumer, or anti-money-laundering authorization potentially applicable to a virtual-office, commercial-mail-receiving, or document-scanning business.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is a separate legal person and is ordinarily subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax on its taxable profits. The standard Corporate Income Tax rate is generally 25%, subject to applicable reduced rates, temporary measures, turnover-based rules, newly incorporated entity rules, and special regimes. The company is not fiscally transparent merely because it has limited liability or non-resident shareholders. Spanish VAT is assessed separately from corporate income tax. The company's tax residence is generally in Spain if it is incorporated under Spanish law, has its registered office in Spain, or has its effective management in Spain, subject to applicable tax treaties.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not operate a United States-style check-the-box election for Spanish limited companies. An SL cannot elect to be treated as a fiscally transparent entity solely by filing a classification form. Transparency may arise only under specific statutory regimes, such as certain entities covered by the Spanish special regime for income attribution, which ordinarily does not apply to a standard SL. Available regime elections or applications may include tax consolidation for qualifying corporate groups, the special regime for mergers, demergers and other qualifying reorganizations, the special cash-accounting regime for VAT, the special regime for travel agencies, and other sector-specific VAT or Corporate Income Tax regimes where statutory conditions are met. Spanish hybrid-mismatch rules implement applicable EU anti-tax-avoidance requirements and generally operate as mandatory denial or inclusion rules rather than elective classification elections. Any election or regime application must be made through the applicable AEAT filing and within the statutory deadlines.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA), the Spanish value added tax system, based principally on Law 37/1992 and its implementing regulations. Mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands apply Spanish VAT. The Canary Islands apply the separate Impuesto General Indirecto Canario (IGIC), and Ceuta and Melilla are outside the territorial scope of EU VAT. A Spanish SL carrying on an economic activity has a Spanish VAT nexus when it makes supplies located in Spain under the place-of-supply rules, imports goods, makes intra-Community acquisitions, or is otherwise required to account for Spanish VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general Spanish VAT turnover threshold exempts a person carrying on an economic activity from registration. A taxable person must register in the census of entrepreneurs, professionals and withholders before commencing taxable activities, making supplies, acquiring goods or services requiring registration, or receiving certain cross-border supplies. The threshold amount is therefore not applicable; statutory registration is generally activity-based rather than based on a minimum annual turnover. Reduced VAT rates of 10% and 4%, and exemptions, may apply to specifically listed supplies. A virtual-office, commercial-mail-receiving, and digital-scanning service will ordinarily be taxable at 21% when its place of supply is Spain, subject to the detailed place-of-supply and exemption rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not currently impose a universal real-time pre-clearance requirement for every business-to-business invoice. Invoices must comply with Spanish invoicing rules, including required supplier and customer identification, NIF where applicable, invoice number and date, description, taxable base, applicable rate, VAT amount, and legally required special statements. The Immediate Supply of Information system (Suministro Inmediato de Información or SII) applies mandatorily to specified taxpayers, principally taxpayers with an annual turnover exceeding EUR 6 million, VAT groups, and taxpayers under the monthly refund regime, with voluntary entry available subject to the rules. SII taxpayers report specified invoice-register data electronically to AEAT, generally within four calendar days, subject to statutory exclusions and transport-related timing rules. Electronic invoicing is mandatory for specified public-sector transactions and is being extended to private-sector business-to-business transactions under Law 18/2022, subject to implementing regulations and phased effective dates; the exact compliance date depends on the taxpayer's turnover and the final regulatory timetable. The anticipated VERI*FACTU and non-VERI*FACTU invoicing-system requirements require compliant billing software, integrity, traceability, conservation and anti-tampering controls, but they do not convert every invoice into an AEAT pre-clearance transaction. The company should maintain certified-compatible accounting and invoicing systems, preserve electronic records, and monitor AEAT implementation deadlines before commencing operations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods exported from the Spanish VAT territory to a destination outside the European Union, the supply may be exempt with the right to deduct input VAT, functionally equivalent to zero rating, if the goods leave the EU customs territory and the supplier can substantiate the export with customs evidence and commercial records. The supplier must establish the identity of the purchaser where required, the transport or dispatch outside the EU, the connection between the invoice and the exported goods, and the customs exit result. Intra-Community supplies of goods may qualify for exemption with deduction where the customer is identified for VAT in another EU Member State, the goods are dispatched or transported to that Member State, the required recapitulative statement is filed, and the transaction is supported by prescribed transport evidence. Services require separate analysis and are not automatically zero-rated as exports. Business-to-business services are generally located where the business customer is established, so a qualifying service supplied to a non-Spanish business customer may be outside the scope of Spanish VAT under the general place-of-supply rule, normally with reverse charge in the customer's jurisdiction. Certain services supplied to non-EU customers or connected with goods located outside the EU may be exempt or outside Spanish VAT under specific Spanish VAT place-of-supply provisions. Virtual-office address services, mail receipt, mail scanning, document handling, and electronically supplied services must be analyzed by customer status, actual use and enjoyment, contractual scope, customer establishment, and the applicable anti-abuse and special place-of-supply rules. An export treatment should not be applied solely because the customer pays from abroad or because the service is marketed internationally.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic customs export declaration or the applicable export declaration reference, including the customs export movement reference and the electronic confirmation that the goods exited the EU customs territory
Commercial invoice identifying the Spanish supplier, customer, goods, value, VAT treatment, and transaction reference
Transport evidence appropriate to the mode of shipment, such as bill of lading, air waybill, CMR consignment note, courier record, or equivalent carrier documentation
Packing list and proof linking the transported goods to the relevant invoice and customs declaration
Proof of delivery or destination evidence where necessary to demonstrate that the goods reached the non-EU destination
Sales contract, purchase order, dispatch instructions, and customer correspondence supporting the export transaction
Evidence of customs exit or other legally accepted export proof retained in the supplier's VAT records
For intra-Community goods supplies, the customer's valid EU VAT number, transport evidence, and required EC Sales List information

Bank payment records may support the transaction but are not generally a substitute for customs exit evidence, and Spain does not generally require an Inward Remittance Certificate as a condition for VAT export exemption

For offshore services, the contract, customer VAT or tax identification details, customer establishment evidence, service-delivery records, invoices, payment evidence, and documentation supporting the applicable place-of-supply conclusion
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spain has no general statutory requirement that export proceeds be repatriated within 180 days as a condition for VAT export exemption. Export VAT treatment is substantiated principally by customs exit, transport, contractual, invoicing, and accounting evidence. AEAT may deny the exemption or refund, assess the unpaid VAT, impose compensatory interest, and impose an administrative penalty where the supplier cannot prove the export, applies an incorrect place-of-supply rule, files inaccurate returns, or claims input VAT that is not deductible. VAT penalty percentages depend on the infringement and circumstances; serious or very serious improper tax treatment may result in penalties commonly ranging from 50% to 150% of the improperly unpaid or refunded tax, subject to statutory aggravating or mitigating rules. Unjustified VAT refunds may be recovered with interest and penalties. Customs non-compliance may trigger customs debt, import VAT, duties, administrative sanctions, and loss or suspension of simplified procedures under the Union Customs Code and Spanish implementing rules. Deliberate tax fraud may also create criminal exposure where the amount defrauded exceeds the applicable Criminal Code threshold, generally EUR 120,000 for a tax period and tax. VAT books, invoices, customs records, transport documents and supporting evidence should be retained for the applicable statutory periods, with the ordinary Spanish tax limitation period generally four years, subject to interruption, special rules, and longer retention periods under accounting, corporate, customs, or litigation requirements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España, operating within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank framework. Foreign-investment reporting is principally administered by the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise. Anti-money-laundering supervision and suspicious-transaction reporting are principally administered through SEPBLAC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain uses the euro and is fully integrated into the European Union single market and SEPA. Current-account transactions, including payments for services, imports, exports, royalties, dividends, interest, and ordinary profit remittances, are generally freely convertible and transferable without general exchange-control approval. Capital-account transactions, including foreign ownership, capital contributions, intercompany loans, acquisitions, and disposals, are generally permitted without prior exchange authorization, subject to applicable foreign-investment filings, beneficial-ownership identification, sanctions controls, anti-money-laundering requirements, tax rules, and any exceptional screening applicable to strategic sectors or public-order concerns. Dividends and other profit distributions require distributable profits, approval under Spanish corporate law, proper accounting records, withholding-tax analysis, and evidence of the recipient's tax status. Banks may require corporate resolutions, audited or management accounts, tax certificates, invoices, contracts, proof of source of funds, and evidence of the legal basis for each cross-border transfer. Transfers involving high-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned parties, unexplained third-party payors, or virtual-office activity without demonstrable operating substance may be delayed or rejected.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no general statutory obligation requiring an exporter to surrender export proceeds to a bank, convert a specified percentage into euros, or repatriate proceeds within a universal statutory deadline. Export receipts may generally remain in foreign-currency accounts or be converted at the holder's discretion, subject to bank contractual terms, accounting requirements, tax rules, sanctions screening, and payment-services controls. Exporters must retain commercial and transport documentation and comply with applicable customs, VAT, Intrastat, statistical, and financial-reporting obligations. Banks may request evidence of the underlying transaction, including invoices, contracts, customs records, bills of lading, delivery evidence, and payment references. Any applicable Banco de España statistical reporting obligation depends on the transaction and reporting framework in force; it is not a currency-surrender requirement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; Capital Contribution Account or temporary capital-deposit arrangement where required by the notary, incorporation process, or bank policy
Operational Account; Capital Contribution Account or temporary capital-deposit arrangement where required by the incorporation process
Operational Account; Capital Contribution Account or temporary capital-deposit arrangement where required by bank policy
Operational Account; Capital Contribution Account or temporary capital-deposit arrangement where required by bank policy

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment collection and treasury support, but low as a substitute for a Spanish operating bank where the company requires local IBAN functionality, corporate cash management, cash deposits, bank guarantees, trade finance, or payment processing for third-party mail and scanning customers. An electronic-money institution or payment institution authorized in an EEA state may provide services in Spain through applicable passporting arrangements and must comply with PSD2, safeguarding, AML, sanctions, operational-resilience, and customer-due-diligence requirements. A non-EEA offshore EMI cannot lawfully provide regulated payment or e-money services into Spain merely through a website or foreign account; it requires an appropriate EU authorization, establishment, agent, or other legally valid access route. Customer funds must not be commingled with the SL's operating funds. Card acquiring and recurring billing should be contracted with a regulated acquirer or payment service provider, with clear merchant-of-record, chargeback, refund, data-protection, and customer-funds arrangements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law does not impose a universal rule that all directors must appear physically at a bank branch. Remote onboarding may be permitted where the bank accepts qualified electronic identification, video identification, certified corporate documents, and reliable verification of directors and ultimate beneficial owners. In practice, banks may require a branch meeting, live video interview, notarized or apostilled documents, Spanish tax identification numbers, proof of Spanish address, and evidence of a genuine operating presence. At least one authorized signatory should be prepared to complete enhanced due diligence. A virtual-office business should expect additional questioning regarding premises, mail custody, customer authorization, privacy controls, chain of custody, staffing, source of customer funds, and the distinction between the company's own revenues and client property.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear or layered ownership involving non-resident shareholders, nominee shareholders, trusts, or entities in multiple jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified constitutional documents for every ownership layer; current shareholder registers; group ownership chart identifying every individual ultimate beneficial owner; passports and residential evidence for beneficial owners, directors, and authorized signatories; notarized powers of attorney where applicable; tax identification numbers; corporate resolutions; and an explanation of the commercial purpose of the ownership structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Virtual-office or commercial-mail-receiving activity perceived as facilitating shell companies, fraud, identity misuse, or third-party financial flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan; Spanish premises lease or service agreement; operating procedures for mail receipt, scanning, forwarding, identity verification, customer authorization, retention, destruction, and incident escalation; customer acceptance policy; prohibited-use policy; sample service agreements; customer due-diligence workflow; staffing and technology evidence; data-protection controls; law-enforcement cooperation protocol; and a transaction-flow diagram demonstrating that customer funds are not held or transferred on behalf of customers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared business activity and expected account turnover, payment corridors, counterparties, or card transactions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved financial model; revenue forecast by product and geography; customer concentration analysis; sample invoices; signed customer contracts; expected monthly transaction volumes; payment-rail explanation; refund and chargeback policy; accounting records; VAT registrations where applicable; and periodic management accounts reconciling banking activity to commercial activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital from an offshore shareholder or related party with insufficient source-of-funds or source-of-wealth evidence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder funding resolution; subscription agreement or intercompany loan agreement; bank statements showing accumulation of funds; audited financial statements; tax returns or tax residence certificates; sale-of-asset documents, dividend records, or financing documents supporting wealth origin; sanctions screening evidence; and a written explanation of the transfer purpose and expected use.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, unrelated third-party payors, cash deposits, cryptocurrency proceeds, or rapid pass-through transfers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written prohibition on personal and third-party accounts; payment acceptance matrix; customer and payor reconciliation; source-of-funds records; documented exception approvals; cash-handling policy; blockchain analytics and regulated-provider records for any digital-asset exposure; enhanced monitoring rules; and evidence that refunds are made only to the original verified payer unless legally justified.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving sanctioned, embargoed, high-risk, or unusually opaque jurisdictions, or counterparties with adverse media
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions and adverse-media screening policy; screening logs for customers, beneficial owners, payors, and beneficiaries; geographic-risk classification; enhanced due-diligence reports; contractual representations; proof of goods or services; end-user and end-use information; escalation records; and documented rejection or blocking procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed person, close associate, senior public official, or high-risk beneficial owner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP identification result; senior-management approval; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; expected-activity profile; enhanced monitoring plan; periodic review schedule; and documented rationale for accepting or continuing the relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to verify Spanish operating address, management control, employees, technology, or actual business activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial lease or serviced-office agreement; utility or occupancy evidence; municipal or tax registrations; employment or contractor records; insurance; website and customer materials; equipment and software invoices; contracts with scanning, courier, shredding, and IT suppliers; management biographies; and photographs or inspection evidence where requested.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Weak governance over personal data and confidential mail, creating fraud, privacy, or regulatory concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: GDPR compliance framework; records of processing activities; controller-processor analysis; customer privacy notices; data-processing agreements; access-control matrix; encryption policy; audit logs; employee confidentiality agreements; breach-response plan; retention schedule; secure destruction certificates; and documented physical and logical segregation of customer information.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route shareholder equity through a regulated bank to the SL's Spanish corporate account, using the investor's account rather than a personal or unrelated third-party account. The transfer narrative should identify the legal nature of the payment, such as share capital subscription, share premium, shareholder contribution, or documented intercompany loan. Before or promptly after receipt, maintain the subscription agreement, shareholder or board resolution, bank payment confirmation, beneficial-owner evidence, source-of-funds file, and accounting entry. For a share-capital increase, complete the Spanish notarial and Commercial Registry formalities and obtain the relevant corporate and tax documentation. Review foreign-investment reporting under the Spanish foreign-investment regime, including any filing required for non-resident investment in a Spanish company; the requirement depends on investor, transaction, sector, value, and applicable exemptions. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments where available and SWIFT for non-SEPA or foreign-currency payments. The receiving bank may require a purpose description, UBO declaration, source-of-funds evidence, sanctions clearance, and confirmation that the funds are not customer money. Convert foreign currency through the bank or an authorized payment provider only after the funds and purpose have cleared compliance review. Do not route capital through customer collections, card processors, personal accounts, or an offshore EMI omnibus account without clear legal ownership and safeguarding analysis.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the SEPA area. Use SWIFT MT103 or its current ISO 20022 successor message for non-SEPA cross-border wires, with complete originator, beneficiary, intermediary-bank, invoice, and purpose information. For material imports or supplier-risk exposure, use a commercial documentary letter of credit issued or confirmed by a regulated bank, supported by the purchase contract, pro forma invoice, shipping documents, insurance documents, customs information, and sanctions or dual-use review. Documentary collections may be used where the counterparty risk is acceptable. Supplier payments should match approved purchase orders, invoices, delivery evidence, and the accounting ledger. For recurring operational expenses, use controlled bank transfers, SEPA direct debit mandates, or corporate cards subject to spending limits. Maintain segregation between operating payments and customer-related funds, and retain payment, invoice, customs, VAT, and delivery records for the applicable Spanish accounting, tax, AML, and audit periods. Banks may reject payments lacking a credible underlying trade or service rationale, particularly where the beneficiary is unrelated to the contracting supplier or located in a high-risk jurisdiction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward exchange contracts with a regulated bank or authorized investment firm, limited to documented forecast or committed foreign-currency exposures and supported by a board-approved treasury policy.

Non-deliverable forwards where the relevant currency is restricted or non-deliverable, provided the counterparty is appropriately regulated, the contract is documented under suitable master terms, the exposure and settlement mechanics are understood, and the arrangement does not circumvent applicable exchange controls.

Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps for documented funding or balance-sheet exposures, subject to counterparty-credit approval, collateral and margin terms, valuation controls, EMIR-related obligations where applicable, and accounting treatment under the company's financial-reporting framework.
Foreign-currency spot conversions for ordinary operating, trade, tax, payroll, and repatriation needs through regulated banks or payment institutions.

Currency options or option-based collars for defined commercial exposures, subject to suitability, cost, valuation, disclosure, board authorization, and controls against speculative or leveraged positions.

Treasury controls should include a written hedging policy, exposure forecasts, authorized counterparties, transaction limits, segregation of dealing and settlement duties, independent valuation, confirmations, collateral monitoring, hedge-accounting assessment, sanctions screening, and periodic board reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts (Cuentas Anuales) filed with the Mercantile Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Central / Provincial Mercantile Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of approval by the general shareholders' meeting; must be filed within 6 months after fiscal year end (December 31 for calendar year entities). Approval must occur within 6 months after year-end, filing within 1 month of approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty up to EUR 1,200 for each late filing (plus continued daily penalties); failure for 2 consecutive fiscal years triggers closure of the mercantile registry sheet and administrative dissolution risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Modelo 200 / short-form Modelo 100)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the 6-month post year-end period; for calendar year entities, from July 1 to July 25 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Surcharge regime: 5% of tax due (charged after 3 months), plus late payment interest; penalties range from 50% to 150% of the deficiency depending on gravity; administrative strike-off not directly used for tax filing but chronic non-filing leads to tax enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Confirmation / Updated Beneficial Ownership Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil as delegated by the Ministry of Justice / UBO registry under Spanish Law 10/2010
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of any change in beneficial ownership; annual confirmation exercise required as part of filing annual accounts or whenever the ownership structure is updated. Mandatory continuous compliance calendar.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance is an infraction under anti-money laundering law with fines up to EUR 100,000 (or 5% of turnover); repeated failure may lead to temporary suspension of voting rights associated with shares and registration blocks.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registry Legalisation of Statutory Books (Libros Registro)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months following the close of the financial year; for calendar year entities, before July 31 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to legalise books does not itself cause strike-off but constitutes a corporate fault; the company is denied registration of certain filings and may incur a registry fine up to EUR 1,200.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit for entities exceeding (on two consecutive years) at least two of the following three thresholds: balance sheet total EUR 2,846,000; annual turnover EUR 5,700,000; average headcount 50 employees. Also mandatory for companies that meet the Audit Law scale or operate under regulated sectors; virtual office/mail scanning services typically remain below thresholds unless group consolidation applies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Plan General de Contabilidad (PGC), compatible and substantially converged with IFRS (EU-adopted); larger groups prepare consolidated statements under IFRS as adopted by EU.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain an internal Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (RTUB) and file any modifications with the Mercantile Registry within one month of occurrence. Annually, the register must be refreshed and reconciled in the meeting of shareholders and reflected in the Annual Accounts certification. Spanish law requires declaration of ownership structure, percentage, and identification of every UBO; any non-compliance triggers anti-money laundering sanctions and registration suspension.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro Registro de Consejeros / Administradores)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Typical annual fee range in Spain for SL registered office and compliance agent service: USD 800 to USD 2,500
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Typical certified audit fee range for an SL if statutory audit thresholds are met: USD 2,500 to USD 8,000; if below thresholds, zero legal audit cost (only intermediate review optional).

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 25% base rate with incentives for R&D investments, innovation activities, and certain sectors under Law 27/2014

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 100 - Annual Corporate Income Tax Return filed electronically through the AEAT portal (www.aeat.es)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 25th day of the month following the end of the tax period (e.g., 25 January for calendar year taxpayers)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable net income before deductions and adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents report only Spanish-source income; apply any treaty-based relief directly or via TRC

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions, tax credits, and special regimes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim applicable deductions and withholdings; non-residents may offset foreign taxes under DTAs

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: 100 euros per day of delay, maximum 1,500 euros for administrative infractions; criminal penalties apply for serious evasion

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain and submit a Treaty Relief Certificate (TRC) to AEAT to claim reduced or zero Spanish WHT on dividends under applicable Double Tax Agreements (DTAs)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 19% statutory rate, reduced to 0-10% under most DTAs; Interest: 19% statutory rate, reduced to 0% under many DTAs if beneficial ownership and arm's length conditions are satisfied

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: 250,000 EUR (triggers mandatory Local File and Master File documentation for related-party transactions)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain implements Economic Substance requirements for certain entities including holding companies and IP vehicles; non-compliance may result in recharacterization of transactions and denial of tax benefits

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting taxable income or inflating deductible expenses to understate the tax base
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines equal to 100% of the evaded tax plus criminal imprisonment ranging from 6 months to 6 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for tax debts; possible disqualification from corporate management, additional fines, and imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a company without genuine economic activity or sufficient substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative dissolution, back payment of taxes, and fines up to 300,000 euros
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for unpaid taxes and potential criminal liability for fraudulent incorporation or management

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to comply with anti-money laundering reporting obligations or KYC requirements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines from 300,000 to 2 million euros or higher, possible revocation of operating license
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability, substantial fines, and imprisonment for aggravated violations
